newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's state oil firm hit by strike, rebels.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's state oil firm hit by strike, rebels.

text.p: Colombia's state oil company was in disarray on Friday after a wildcat strike erupted in a major production centre in the country's north and suspected leftist rebels blew up the country's main oil pipeline.

Reports on the effectiveness of the strike in Barrancabermeja, an industrial city in northern Santander province, were sketchy since strikers managed to shut down the Bogota headquarters of Ecopetrol, the state oil company.

But Cesar Carrillo, a leader of the 6,000-strong state oil workers union known as USO, said the strike began at midnight on Thursday (0500 GMT on Friday) and that it had paralysed most refinery and oil pumping operations in the city on the banks of Colombia's Magdalena river.
Speaking in a telephone interview, Carrillo said the strike would last "indefinitely" and it was called to protest against the killing of USO vice president Rafael Gonzalez.
Gonzalez, who owned a restaurant in Barrancabermeja, was slain by a lone gunmen who entered the establishment on Thursday evening, police said.
"It was a crime of the state," Carrillo said, alleging that Gonzalez had been killed because of USO's longstanding opposition to foreign oil companies operating in Colombia.
William Giraldo, chief spokesman for Ecopetrol, said he was unable to confirm the extent of the work stoppage in Barrancabermeja, which is home to the country's leading oil refinery.

But he said Ecopetrol's problems had been compounded by a suspected guerrilla attack on the Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline, which carries 220,000 barrels of oil per day from the Cano Limon fields operated by Occidental Petroleum Corp to the Caribbean port of Covenas.

The initial bomb explosion, early on Thursday near the northern city of Cucuta on Colombia's border with Venezuela, was followed by a second accidental blast hours later in which one member of an emergency repair crew was killed, Girlado said.
He said Ecopetrol hoped to complete repair work and resume pumping operations by late Friday on the pipeline, which has been bombed more than 40 times this year.
